validated_results.title: Dietary total and insoluble fiber intakes are inversely associated with prostate cancer risk.
validated_results.reason: Prospective cohort of 3313 men reporting incident prostate cancer risk by quartile of energy-adjusted total dietary fiber intake, a target dietary exposure with a separable incidence estimate.

extraction.comparison_type: quartile 4 vs quartile 1 of energy-adjusted total dietary fiber intake
extraction.timing: diagnosed between 1994 and 2007, median follow-up 12.6 y
extraction.population: 3313 men from the SU.VI.MAX cohort who completed at least 3 24-h dietary records

sample_size.excerpt: This prospective analysis included 3313 men from the Supplémentation en Vitamines et Minéraux Antioxydants (SU.VI.MAX) cohort who completed at least 3 24-h dietary records.

effect_size.excerpt: Prostate cancer risk was inversely associated with total dietary fiber intake (HR of quartile 4 vs. quartile 1 = 0.47; 95% CI: 0.27, 0.81; P = 0.001), insoluble (HR = 0.46; 95% CI: 0.27, 0.78; P = 0.001), and legume (HR = 0.55; 95% CI: 0.32, 0.95; P = 0.04) fiber intakes.

comparison.excerpt: Associations between quartiles of energy-adjusted dietary fiber intake and prostate cancer risk

timing.excerpt: diagnosed between 1994 and 2007 (median follow-up of 12.6 y)

continent.excerpt: Supplémentation en Vitamines et Minéraux Antioxydants (SU.VI.MAX) cohort

validated_results.title: Alcohol intake increases high-grade prostate cancer risk among men taking dutasteride in the REDUCE trial.
validated_results.reason: Randomized trial participants with baseline alcohol intake questionnaires and biopsy-determined incident prostate cancer, with a separable alcohol-specific estimate reported.

extraction.comparison_type: more than seven drinks per week vs lower/no alcohol intake, among men randomized to dutasteride, high-grade (Gleason >7) PCa
extraction.design: secondary analysis of a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial (observational alcohol exposure)
extraction.timing: 4-yr trial with biopsy at 2 yr and 4 yr of follow-up; alcohol intake determined at baseline
extraction.population: 6374 men with baseline prostate-specific antigen between 2.5 and 10.0 ng/ml and a recent negative prostate biopsy

sample_size.excerpt: Of 6374 participants in our analysis, approximately 25% reported no alcohol consumption, 49% were moderate drinkers (one to seven drinks per week), and 26% were heavy drinkers (more than seven drinks per week).

effect_size.excerpt: In contrast, men randomized to dutasteride and reporting more than seven drinks per week were 86% more likely to be diagnosed with high-grade PCa (p=0.01). Among alcohol abstainers, dutasteride was associated with significantly reduced risk of high-grade PCa (OR: 0.59; 95% CI, 0.38-0.90), but dutasteride was no longer associated with reduced high-grade PCa among men reporting high alcohol intake (OR: 0.99; 95% CI, 0.67-1.45).
